en: Thus have I heard— The Mahāgosiṅga Sutta, Discourse at Gosiṅga Sal Wood, from the Majjhima Nikāya.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in the Gosīṅga Sāla-tree Grove together with many well-known and renowned elder disciples:
the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, the Venerable Anuruddha,
the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Ānanda, and other well-known and renowned elders.

Together with those disciples, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having emerged from seclusion in the evening, approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached him, he said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa:
"Come, friend Kassapa, let us go to the Venerable Sāriputta to listen to the Dhamma."
“Yes, friend,” the Venerable Mahākassapa replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna.
Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, and the Venerable Anuruddha approached the Venerable Sāriputta in order to hear the Dhamma.
The Venerable Ānanda saw the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, and the Venerable Anuruddha approaching the Venerable Sāriputta to hear the Dhamma.
Having seen them, he approached the Venerable Revata and, having approached, said this to the Venerable Revata:
"Friend Revata, those good men who were approaching the Venerable Sāriputta were doing so to hear the Dhamma.
Come, friend Revata, let us approach the Venerable Sāriputta to hear the Dhamma."
“Yes, friend,” the Venerable Revata replied to the Venerable Ānanda.
Then the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda approached the Venerable Sāriputta in order to hear the Dhamma.
The Venerable Sāriputta saw the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda coming from afar.
Having seen him, he said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Let the Venerable Ānanda come.
Welcome to the Venerable Ānanda, the attendant of the Blessed One, who dwells in the presence of the Blessed One."
“Friend Ānanda, the Gosiṅga Sāla forest is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom. Divine, as it were, fragrances are wafting about.
In what kind of way, friend Ānanda, would a bhikkhu make the Gosiṅga Sāla forest shine?
“In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu is learned, one who has retained what he has heard, and one who has accumulated what he has heard. Those teachings...”
They are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end; they are meaningful and well-phrased, and they proclaim a holy life that is entirely complete and pure.
Such teachings as these he has heard much of, retained, mastered verbally, examined with the mind, and thoroughly penetrated through right view.
Thus he teaches the Dhamma to the four assemblies with well-rounded words and phrases, coherently linked, for the uprooting of the underlying tendencies.
It is by such a bhikkhu, friend Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Revata:
“Friend Revata, the Venerable Ānanda has already spoken according to his own inspiration.
Now, we shall ask the Venerable Revata:
‘Friend Revata, delightful is the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove! It is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom; it seems as if divine fragrances are wafting about.’”
“Friend Revata, what kind of bhikkhu would beautify the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove?
“Here, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu delights in seclusion, rejoices in seclusion, is devoted to internal tranquility of mind, does not neglect jhāna, possesses insight, and frequents empty huts.
It is such a bhikkhu, friend Sāriputta, who would beautify the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.”
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Anuruddha:
"Friend Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata has already explained according to his own inspiration.
Now, we ask the Venerable Anuruddha about this."
“‘Friend Anuruddha, beautiful is the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove! It is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom; I imagine divine fragrances are wafting about.
Friend Anuruddha, what kind of bhikkhu would make the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove shine?
‘In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu surveys a thousand worlds with the purified divine eye, which surpasses the human.’”
“Just as, friend Sāriputta, a man with good eyesight, having gone to the top of a magnificent palace, might look down upon a thousand wheel-rims;
even so, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, looks down upon a thousand worlds.
It is by such a bhikkhu, friend Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.”
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahākassapa:
"Friend Kassapa, the Venerable Anuruddha has already given his answer according to his own inspiration.
Now, we ask the Venerable Mahākassapa about this matter."
“Friend Kassapa, the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and the sāla trees are in full bloom. Divine, as it were, are the fragrances wafting about.
In what manner, friend Kassapa, would a bhikkhu beautify the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove?
“In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu himself dwells in the forest and speaks in praise of dwelling in the forest.”
He himself is an alms-food eater and speaks in praise of the practice of eating alms-food;
he himself is a wearer of rag-robes and speaks in praise of the practice of wearing rag-robes; he himself possesses only the three robes and speaks in praise of possessing only the three robes;
he himself is of few desires and speaks in praise of having few desires; he himself is contented...
He himself is content and speaks in praise of contentment; he himself is secluded and speaks in praise of seclusion;
he himself is unassociated with society and speaks in praise of non-association; he himself has aroused energy and speaks in praise of the arousal of energy;
he himself is perfected in virtue and speaks in praise of the perfection of virtue.
He himself is accomplished in concentration and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of concentration;
he himself is accomplished in wisdom and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of wisdom; he himself is accomplished in liberation and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of liberation;
he himself is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation.
“Indeed, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu such as this would illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:
“Friend Moggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa has given his answer according to his own inspiration.”
In this regard, we now ask the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:
“Friend Moggallāna, delightful is the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove! It is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom; it seems as if divine fragrances are wafting about.
In what manner, friend Moggallāna, would a bhikkhu make the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove shine?”
“Here, friend Sāriputta, two bhikkhus engage in a discussion on the Abhidhamma;
they ask each other questions, and being asked questions by one another, they answer them without faltering,
and their discourse proceeds in accordance with the Dhamma.”
“Indeed, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu such as this would illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said to the Venerable Sāriputta:
“Friend Sāriputta, we have all spoken according to our own inspiration.”
In this regard, we now ask the Venerable Sāriputta:
“Friend Sāriputta, the Gosiṅga Sāl forest is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom, so that, I imagine, divine fragrances are wafting about.
In what manner, friend Sāriputta, would a bhikkhu illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāl forest?”
“Here, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu wields mastery over his mind, and he does not let himself be wielded by the mind.
Whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in during the morning, in that meditative attainment he dwells during the morning;
whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in during the midday, in that meditative attainment he dwells during the midday.”
Whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the evening, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the evening.
Just as if, friend Moggallāna, a king or a king’s high minister had a chest full of various colored garments:
whatever pair of garments he might desire to put on in the morning, that very pair of garments he would put on in the morning.
Whatever pair of robes he might wish to put on at midday, that very pair of robes he would put on at midday;
whatever pair of robes he might wish to put on in the evening, that very pair of robes he would put on in the evening.
In the same way, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu wields mastery over his mind; he does not act under the sway of his mind.
Thus, whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the morning, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the morning;
whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the midday, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the midday;
whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the evening, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the evening.
“Indeed, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu such as this would illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
Then the Venerable Sāriputta said to those venerable ones:
“Friends, we have all given our own individual explanations according to our inspiration.”
"Come, friends, let us approach the Blessed One; having approached, we shall report this matter to the Blessed One.
We will bear it in mind exactly as the Blessed One explains it.
"So be it, friend," those venerable ones replied to the venerable Sāriputta.

Then those venerable ones approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. As they were sitting there, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One:
“Just now, Bhante, the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda approached me for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma.
I saw, Bhante, the Venerable Revata and the Venerable Ānanda coming from afar.”
Having seen him, I said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Come, Venerable Ānanda.
Welcome to the Venerable Ānanda, the attendant of the Blessed One, who dwells in the presence of the Blessed One."
“Friend Ānanda, the Gosiṅga Sāla grove is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom. Divine, as it were, fragrances are wafting about.
In what kind of way, friend Ānanda, would a bhikkhu make the Gosiṅga Sāla grove shine?
When this was said, Bhante, the Venerable Ānanda said this to me:
“Here, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu is learned, a bearer of the Dhamma...
[as above] ...for the uprooting of the underlying tendencies.
It is by such a bhikkhu, friend Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.”
“Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta!
It is just as Ānanda himself would answer correctly when explaining it.
For Ānanda, Sāriputta, is learned, a bearer of what he has heard, and a storehouse of what he has heard. Those teachings which are beautiful in the beginning...”
They are beautiful in the middle and beautiful at the end, meaningful and well-phrased; they proclaim a holy life that is entirely complete and pure.
Such teachings as these he has heard much of, retained, mastered through speech, examined with the mind, and thoroughly penetrated by view.
“Thus he teaches the Dhamma to the four assemblies with well-rounded words and phrases, coherently linked, for the uprooting of the underlying tendencies.
When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the venerable Revata:
“Friend Revata, the venerable Ānanda has given his answer according to his own inspiration.”
In this regard, we now ask the Venerable Revata:
“Friend Revata, the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and all the sāla trees are in full bloom, as if divine fragrances are wafting about.
In what manner, friend Revata, would a bhikkhu make the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove shine?”
When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Revata said this to me:

“In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu delights in seclusion, rejoices in seclusion, is devoted to internal tranquility of mind, does not neglect jhāna, possesses insight, and frequents empty huts.
It is by such a bhikkhu as this, friend Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.”
“Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta!
It is just as Revata would answer if he were answering correctly.

For Revata, Sāriputta, delights in seclusion and rejoices in seclusion; he is devoted to internal mental tranquility, has not cast off the jhānas, is endowed with insight, and is one who cultivates empty huts.”
“When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Anuruddha:
‘Friend Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata has already answered...
[as before] ...In what kind of way, friend Anuruddha, would a bhikkhu illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove?’”
When this was said, venerable sir, the Venerable Anuruddha said this to me:
“In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu surveys a thousand worlds with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans.
Just as, friend Sāriputta, a man with good sight... [as above] ...”
“Friend Sāriputta, it is indeed with such a bhikkhu as this that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would shine.
“Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta! It is just as Anuruddha himself would rightly declare when he speaks.
For Anuruddha, Sāriputta, surveys a thousand worlds with his purified divine eye, which surpasses that of humans.”
“When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Mahākassapa:
‘Friend Kassapa, the Venerable Anuruddha has already given his answer according to his own inspiration.
Now we ask the Venerable Mahākassapa... [and so on].
“Friend Kassapa, what kind of bhikkhu would illuminate this Gosiṅga Sāla Grove?
When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Mahākassapa said this to me:
“In this case, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu is himself a forest-dweller and speaks in praise of being a forest-dweller;”

He himself is an alms-food eater …pe… he himself is a wearer of rag-robes …pe… he himself is a wearer of the three robes …pe… he himself is one of few desires …pe… he himself is contented …pe… he himself is secluded …pe… he himself is unassociated with the crowd …pe… he himself is one who has aroused energy …pe… he himself...

And he is himself accomplished in virtue …pe… he is himself accomplished in concentration …pe… he is himself accomplished in wisdom … he is himself accomplished in liberation … he is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation,
and he speaks in praise of the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation.
“Indeed, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu such as this would illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
“Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta!
It is just as Kassapa himself would have answered, had he been answering correctly.”
For Kassapa, Sāriputta, is himself a forest-dweller and speaks in praise of forest-dwelling;
he is himself an alms-food eater and speaks in praise of eating almsfood; he is himself a wearer of rag-robes and speaks in praise of wearing rag-robes;
he is himself a wearer of the three robes and speaks in praise of wearing the three robes; and he is himself one of few desires.
He speaks in praise of fewness of desires and is himself content; he speaks in praise of contentment and is himself contented;
he speaks in praise of seclusion and is himself secluded; he speaks in praise of non-association and is himself unassociated;
he speaks in praise of the arousal of energy and is himself energetic; he speaks in praise of the perfection of virtue and is himself perfected in virtue.
“He himself possesses concentration and speaks in praise of the possession of concentration;
he himself possesses wisdom and speaks in praise of the possession of wisdom; he himself possesses liberation and speaks in praise of the possession of liberation;
he himself possesses the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks in praise of the possession of the knowledge and vision of liberation.”
“When this was said, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:
‘Friend Moggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa has already given his answer according to his own inspiration.
Now, friend Moggallāna, we ask you... [and so on].
“Friend Moggallāna, what kind of bhikkhu would make the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove shine?
When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to me:
“In this case, friend Sāriputta, two bhikkhus are engaged in a discussion on the Abhidhamma. They pose questions to one another...”
They ask questions of one another and, being questioned, they provide answers without faltering,
and their discourse proceeds in accordance with the Dhamma.
It is by such a bhikkhu, friend Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.”
“Excellent, excellent, Sāriputta! It is just as Moggallāna would speak when speaking correctly.
For Moggallāna, Sāriputta, is a preacher of the Dhamma.
When this was said, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to the Blessed One:
“Then, venerable sir, I said to the Venerable Sāriputta:
‘Friends, we have all given our explanations according to our own inspiration.
Now, therefore, we ask the Venerable Sāriputta:’”
“Friend Sāriputta, the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove is delightful; it is a moonlit night, and the sāla trees are in full bloom, so that, I imagine, divine fragrances are wafting about.
In what kind of way, friend Sāriputta, would a bhikkhu beautify the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove?
When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Sāriputta said this to me:
“Here, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu wields mastery over his mind and does not let himself be wielded by the mind.
Whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in during the morning, in that meditative attainment he dwells during the morning;
whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in during the midday, in that meditative attainment he dwells during the midday.”
With whatever dwelling-attainment he wishes to dwell in during the evening, with that dwelling-attainment he dwells in the evening.
Just as if, friend Moggallāna, a king or a king’s high minister had a chest full of various colored garments:

whichever pair of garments he might wish to put on in the morning, that very pair of garments he would put on in the morning; so too, friend Moggallāna, with whatever dwelling-attainment he wishes to dwell in during the evening, with that dwelling-attainment he dwells in the evening.
Whatever pair of robes he might wish to put on at midday, that very pair of robes he would put on at midday;
whatever pair of robes he might wish to put on in the evening, that very pair of robes he would put on in the evening.
In the same way, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu wields mastery over his mind; he does not act under the sway of his mind.
Thus, whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the morning, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the morning;
whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the midday, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the midday;
whatever dwelling-attainment he desires to dwell in during the evening, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the evening.
“Indeed, friend Moggallāna, a bhikkhu such as this would illuminate the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
“Excellent, excellent, Moggallāna!
It is just as Sāriputta would have answered, had he been answering correctly.”
For Sāriputta, Moggallāna, wields mastery over his mind and does not act under the sway of his mind.
Whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in during the morning, in that meditative attainment he dwells during the morning;
whatever meditative attainment he wishes to dwell in at midday, in that meditative attainment he dwells at midday.
“Whatever dwelling-attainment he wishes to dwell in during the evening, in that dwelling-attainment he dwells during the evening.
When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One:
“Whose words, Bhante, are well-spoken?”
“Sāriputta, all that you have said is well-spoken by way of exposition.
Nevertheless, listen also to me as to what kind of bhikkhu would illuminate this Gosiṅga Sāla Grove.
Here, Sāriputta, after returning from his almsround following his meal, a bhikkhu sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness before him:”
‘I shall not break this cross-legged posture until my mind is liberated from the taints through non-clinging.
It is by such a bhikkhu, Sāriputta, that the Gosiṅga Sāla Grove would be illumined.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Those venerable ones were uplifted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.
The second discourse, the Mahāgośṛṅga Sūtra, is finished.
